public_sources.title: Time-sensitive anytime-valid testing
public_sources.used_scope: Finite-horizon anytime-valid testing is a time/wealth control problem for a prescribed alternative; the paper identifies worst-case composite-alternative control as an open extension.

public_sources.title: Optimal e-values for testing the mean of a bounded random variable against a composite alternative
public_sources.used_scope: GROW/REGROW give worst-case log-growth criteria and can behave very differently from finite-horizon detection objectives.

public_sources.title: Strong duality for the GROW criterion
public_sources.used_scope: Background for least-favourable distributions under minimax log-growth; not used as a theorem for the finite-horizon recursion here.

least_favourable_reduction.result: For the two-level upper-tail/floor audit model, true-commit tail probability increases with q_good, so q_good=.60 is least favourable over [.60,.80]. Replacing a null opportunity by a true-improvement opportunity cannot reduce eventual true-commit probability. Therefore the tested minimax over 1-5 true improvements reduces to one q=.60 improvement placed adversarially among 20 positions.
least_favourable_reduction.scope_guard: Fixed fresh-audit schedule; binary candidate class; no candidate-dependent discordance-rate information after audit start.

maximin_recurrence.definition: With current threshold m=1/(alpha*C), null tail p_k, q=.60 tail a_k and c_k=(1-m p_k)/(1-p_k), define R_n(m) as best worst-position true-commit probability normalized by current null-prefix survival.
maximin_recurrence.recurrence: R_1(m)=max_k a_k; R_n(m)=max_k min(a_k,(1-p_k)R_{n-1}(m/c_k)) over valid m p_k<1.
maximin_recurrence.numerics: Log-m DP; r=20 action sequence stable at 5k, 10k and >=20k grid points; reported probabilities then forward-evaluated exactly.
maximin_recurrence.scope_guard: Deterministic two-level upper-tail/floor maps only; predictable randomized/richer maps remain untested.

r20_minimax.policy: k17 for positions 1-15, then k16 for 16-20
r20_minimax.interpretation: Strict one-good q=.60 minimax gain over fixed k17 is only about 0.0001007 absolute while using much more of the error budget. The larger benefit is for stronger or multiple improvements and non-worst placements.
r20_minimax.prior_policy_coincidence: This sequence matches the previous q=.75 prior-weighted Bellman survival path in this tested configuration; this is an empirical/configuration-specific coincidence, not a general Bayes=minimax theorem.

depth_extension.cost_model: Conditional on A launched audits at fixed discordance rate rho, total pairs to collect A*r discordances are negative-binomial; q95 integrates over the random audit count. Candidate-dependent rho and wall-clock parallelism are not modeled.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Finite-horizon maximin control for tail-floor candidate e-values under unknown improvement timing/effect.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Monotonicity reduction, converged DP and exhaustive placement checks.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Deterministic two-level maps; fresh fixed-discordant audits.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Optimize discordant depth jointly with robust power and pair-cost tail risk rather than maximizing raw detection power.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: r=10/20/30/50 maximin policies and negative-binomial mean/q95 costs over rho=.2/.4/.6.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Fixed rho within each cost scenario.

rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected: robust q in [.60,.80] requires full interval search; monotone upper-tail power makes q=.60 least favourable here.
Rejected: unknown 1-5 improvements makes the strict minimax point high-dimensional; in this model one improvement is least favourable.
Narrowed: 15xk17+5xk16 is a large strict minimax improvement over fixed k17; at q=.60,g=1 its absolute gain is only about 0.00010 while all-null FWER rises from about .0255 to .0478.
Rejected: deeper fixed-discordant audits are robustly better just because raw worst-case power rises; low-rho all-null pair cost increases sharply with r.

frontier.action: Solve a constrained robust DP choosing r in {10,20,30,50} and k with rho uncertainty in [0.2,0.6], maximizing worst-position q=.60 true-commit probability under FWER<=.05 and a high-quantile total-pair budget; compare fixed depth with shallow-to-deep switching.
Allow predictable randomized/mixture tail-floor maps and test whether they improve deterministic maximin by equalizing active worst-position constraints without increasing lifetime FWER.
Sweep horizon, alpha, r and q_min to map where prior-weighted and minimax policies diverge.
Replace fixed-rho cost with candidate-dependent/predictably varying discordance-rate bounds and censored fixed-total audits.
Compare finite-horizon worst-position utility against GROW/REGROW-style robustness on the same paired-sign model.

exact_next_action: Derive a constrained robust DP that can choose r in {10,20,30,50} and tail k, maximizes q=.60 single-improvement worst-placement true-commit probability, and enforces all-null FWER<=.05 plus a rho=.20 95th-percentile total-pair budget; compare fixed-depth policies with shallow-to-deep switching.
